summary.headline: Arman Financial Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT hit a record INR51 crore on AUM of INR3,209 crore (up 51% YoY), with cost-to-income down to 42.6%.
summary.overview: Consolidated AUM crossed INR3,000 crore for the first time at INR3,209 crore, up 51% YoY, and disbursements rose 72% YoY to INR818 crore. Profit after tax reached a record INR51 crore versus INR8 crore in Q2 FY26, and H1 PAT of INR97 crore already exceeds the full FY26 PAT of INR57 crore. Asset quality was stable overall (GNPA 2.73%), but management flagged a about 40bp rise in PAR 30-90 in microfinance, drought stress in Maharashtra and Karnataka (7.6% of AUM), and the lapse of CGFMU cover on loans from April 1, 2026 pending scheme renewal.

segments.name: Namra Finance (microfinance subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,424 crore (+61% YoY, +12% QoQ); Q2 disbursement INR654 crore; GTI INR168 crore (+56% YoY); PAT INR34 crore vs loss of INR1 crore; H1 PAT INR63 crore vs FY26 full-year INR13 crore. GNPA 2.59%, NNPA 1.01%, NIM 16.6% (15.37% in Q1), CRAR 37.2%, c.5 lakh active customers.

segments.name: Arman standalone
segments.commentary: AUM INR784 crore (+26% YoY, +3% QoQ); mix MSME c.74%, LAP c.13%, two-wheeler c.12%. Q2 disbursement INR164 crore; GTI INR68 crore (+30% YoY); PPoP INR27 crore; PAT INR17 crore; H1 PAT INR32 crore.

guidance_outlook: Opex-to-AUM target of about 7% by March 2027 (vs peak of c.9-10%); currently at about 8%, management says on track.
Long-run opex-to-AUM view: around 6% would be 'fairly good'; the lowest historical MFI level was c.4.5-4.75%.
Management says INR5,000 crore AUM is achievable within about 18 months; no formal guidance on timing given.
No capital raise needed to reach INR5,000 crore AUM, per management.
Management remains positive on H2 FY27, with Q4 historically the strongest quarter.
Possible CGFMU renewal could bring one-time opex load and provision reversals; management said the outcome is unknowable at this stage.
capex_capacity: Operating model: separated credit and recovery from branch operations; independent credit team for MFI, separate recovery team for branches needing support.
Loans under the new credit structure show c.15% lower default rates than the earlier model (management cautions the true test is the next credit cycle).
Around 110,000 applications processed per month, leading to 25,000-30,000 disbursed customers.
Digital collections: c.49% of microfinance collections via UPI and e-NACH as of Sep 2026; individual lending c.40% of MFI portfolio.
Workforce c.5,200 employees (errata to 5,700) across 11 states.
demand_pricing: Competition: management says smaller players and some large players face difficulty; banks serving MFIs via BC/co-lending have pulled back in certain cases, while fintechs and gold loans compete for rural borrowers.
Good-quality customers face very competitive demand; borrowers with past defaults are hard to lend to.
Rejection rates remain high by design; management says it would rather turn away business than take on future problem customers.
Average ticket size in LAP and MSME fell QoQ; management attributed this to credit policy and risk tolerance, not demand.
Incremental borrowing cost fell to 11.3%; Acuité reaffirmed A- with outlook revised to positive, CARE reaffirmed A- stable.

qa_highlights.question: How is competitive intensity in your geographies, given SFBs pulling back from MFI and small NBFC liquidity stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition persists from fintechs and gold loans, and some large players are struggling too; banks via BC and co-lending have pulled back in some cases, but Arman has no problem accessing bank funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the collection efficiency dip from 96.9% in June to 96.2% in September normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a post-monsoon dip is normal historically; Maharashtra saw some deterioration and Gujarat saw impact from low rainfall; Vivek Modi said the c.40bp PAR 30-90 rise is being watched but not overly worried about, with a delayed drought impact possible.

qa_highlights.question: Does CGFMU non-renewal change strategy, given MFI cover fell from c.90% to 51%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said strategy is unchanged; CGFMU is an insurance layer, not a substitute for underwriting; the company survived 34 years without it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CGFMU renewal and UPI MDR affect provisions, opex and the 7% target?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi said NCGTC indicates a strong likelihood of a policy with delay, and any premium could be P&L-neutral versus provision reversals. On UPI MDR, the company is awaiting industry-level exemption and has not included it in the 7% target.

qa_highlights.question: When will AUM reach INR5,000 crore and what is the opex-to-AUM outlook; is capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR5,000 crore is definitely achievable in about 18 months with compounding; opex-to-AUM around 6% would be good; no capital raise needed while growing near ROE.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Arman standalone provisions decline QoQ (INR5.2 crore to INR4 crore) despite portfolio growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi attributed it to better asset quality, lower write-offs, and a higher LAP share (c.13%, GNPA sub-1.5%) versus unsecured (c.3%); the CGFMU-covered MSME book of c.INR200 crore+ also helps.

risks_watch: CGFMU renewal timing and terms; loans originated from April 1, 2026 are not covered; MFI cover is down to 51% of the portfolio and MSME cover to 30%.
Drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka (7.6% of AUM): Maharashtra fresh delinquencies rose about 1% in October; impact may lag several months.
Possible UPI MDR cost on digital collections if no exemption is granted; the impact is currently unquantified.
Microfinance PAR 30-90 up about 40bp QoQ; management asked investors not to track QoQ basis points.
Opex-to-AUM target of 7% by March 2027 remains at about 8% today; cost trajectory vs growth.
Sustainability of the 15% lower default-rate benefit of the new credit structure, untested through a full credit cycle.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating turnaround and growth, with explicit caution on Maharashtra and Karnataka drought stress, the CGFMU lapse and UPI MDR; management was candid about not having answers on CGFMU terms or MDR, and deflected some questions (e.g., the 'antifragile' theme) with humour.
key_quotes: Q2 has been a particularly strong quarter for Arman.
Our rejection rates remain high, and we are perfectly comfortable with that.
It does not change our strategy, and I think I made that in my kind of said that in my opening remarks as well, that CGFMU was available.
Even today, as far as Arman is concerned, we have no problem accessing bank funding or anything like that.

growth.why: Management guides INR5,000 crore AUM within about 18 months (from INR3,209 crore, roughly 56% higher) and opex-to-AUM to about 7% by March 2027, backed by disbursement growth of 72% YoY and a new credit operating model, but no new capacity, orders or contracts with numbers were given and no formal timing was guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Opex-to-AUM guided from about 8% toward 7% by March 2027 (peak c.9-10%), and Namra NIM rose to 16.6% from 15.37% in Q1, with cost-to-income down to 42.6% from 51.7% peak in Q4 FY26; offset risk from CGFMU and UPI MDR costs is unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM at INR3,209 crore (+51% YoY) with Q2 disbursement INR818 crore (+72% YoY); management says INR5,000 crore is achievable in about 18 months, roughly 56% above current AUM, though no formal timing was guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no capital raise is needed to reach INR5,000 crore AUM, and no new capex or branch expansion was discussed beyond the operating model change.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management remains positive on H2 FY27 with Q4 historically strongest, and H1 PAT of INR97 crore already exceeds full FY26 PAT of INR57 crore, but no formal numeric guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Maharashtra and Karnataka drought stress (7.6% of AUM), PAR 30-90 up about 40bp in microfinance, and CGFMU cover down to 51% for MFI (from c.90%) could pressure provisions, though management calls the CGFMU outcome unknowable.

rows.label: CGFMU renewal and UPI MDR outcome
rows.why: NCGTC indicates strong likelihood of a delayed policy, with any premium possibly P&L-neutral versus provision reversals; UPI MDR exemption pending and excluded from the 7% opex target, impact unquantified.

rows.label: Opex-to-AUM falls to about 7%
rows.why: Opex-to-AUM currently about 8% versus peak c.9-10%, management says on track; cost-to-income already fell to 42.6% from 51.7% in Q4 FY26.

rows.label: Borrowing cost decline and rating upgrade
rows.why: Incremental borrowing cost fell to 11.3% from 11.7% in Q1, and Acuité revised outlook to positive from A- reaffirmed; Arman has no problem accessing bank funding.

tone.note: Management was confident on the turnaround, AUM growth and cost trajectory, but cautious on drought stress, CGFMU renewal terms and UPI MDR; analysts pressed on competition, collection efficiency dip from 96.9% to 96.2%, and provisioning trends.
